dct_description_sm: Recently, thermal erosion processes led to the destruction of ice-wedge polygons and the formation of gullies on Bylot island, Nunavut. The gullies drain the surrounding wetland polygons directly affected by the disturbance and may alter the adjacent wetlands. Another project studies the geomorphological processes of gully formation (Fortier et al., 35 gullies were mapped during 2009 and 2010 surveys). This project focuses on vegetation change and aims to assess: 1) the recurrence of such events in time and space; 2) the vegetation dynamic following the disturbance; and 3) the short and long term impact on the carrying capacity of the lowland.
dct_title_s: Sirmilik National Park, Bylot Island, Nunavut, Canada
